title: Unique Paths
description:
A robot sits in the top-left cell of an `m x n` grid and wants to reach the bottom-right cell. At every step it may move **only right or only down**.

Return how many distinct routes exist from the start to the goal.

examples.explanation: The three routes are Right-Down-Down, Down-Right-Down and Down-Down-Right.
Already at the goal; the empty route counts.

constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: How many ways are there to reach a cell on the top row or the left column? Exactly one.
Any other cell is entered from the cell above it or the cell to its left, so its count is the sum of those two.
You only ever need the previous row, so a single 1-D array of length n is enough. There is also a closed form: choose which of the m+n-2 moves are 'down'.
signature: def uniquePaths(self, m: int, n: int) -> int:
approach:
**Key insight: a cell can only be entered from above or from the left, so its route count is the sum of those two counts.**

Define `dp[i][j]` = number of routes from `(0,0)` to `(i,j)`. Every cell in row 0 or column 0 has exactly one route (a straight line). For the rest, `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]`. The answer is `dp[m-1][n-1]`.

**Why it is correct:** the last move into `(i,j)` is either a Down move from `(i-1,j)` or a Right move from `(i,j-1)`; those two sets of routes are disjoint and together cover every route.

**Space optimisation:** when filling row `i` left to right, `row[j]` still holds the value from row `i-1` (the cell above) and `row[j-1]` already holds the new value (the cell to the left), so `row[j] += row[j-1]` updates in place with O(n) memory.

**Closed form:** every route is a sequence of `m-1` downs and `n-1` rights, so the answer is `C(m+n-2, m-1)`. Compute it incrementally to avoid huge factorials.

**Common mistakes:** forgetting that the 1 x 1 grid has exactly one route; mixing up which index is rows versus columns (the answer is symmetric, so it does not matter here, but it will in Unique Paths II).

**Interview follow-ups:** (1) Add obstacles (Unique Paths II: an obstacle cell gets 0 routes). (2) Allow diagonal moves (add a third term `dp[i-1][j-1]`). (3) Return the number of routes modulo a prime when the grid is large, or derive the combinatorial formula and discuss overflow.
